Major Ion Components

Source: R/geochemistry.R
major_ions.Rd

Calculates aggregated major-ion component concentrations for hydrogeochemical evaluation.

Usage

major_ions(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
major_ions(df, location, analyte, result, unit, sample_date, ...)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
major_ions(df, analyte_matching = c("exact", "strict", "normalized"))

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location

Location identifier column.

analyte

Analyte column.

result

Analytical result column.

unit

Reporting unit column.

sample_date

Sample date column.

analyte_matching

Analyte matching strategy. One of `"exact"`, `"strict"`, or `"normalized"`.

Value

A data frame containing one record per location and sample-date combination.

Details

`major_ions()` is an S3 generic that supports both raw data frames and `env_schema` objects.

For data frames, `major_ions()` first converts the supplied data to an `env_schema` object and then dispatches to [major_ions.env_schema()].

Major-ion concentrations are calculated from analytical results converted to milliequivalents per liter (meq/L).

Output Variables

Returned variables include:

  • `calcium`

  • `magnesium`

  • `sodium`

  • `potassium`

  • `sodium_potassium`

  • `chloride`

  • `sulfate`

  • `alkalinity`

All concentrations are expressed in milliequivalents per liter (meq/L).

Examples

data(gw)

major_ions(gw)
